human_quote: And the other thing is should we consider a new name for the system other than CARR. Thats the name of the company I work for - and if I ever left this company it would be odd to have a system named after said company. It should be independently named
decision_frame: Should the underlying Joe-owned software platform receive an independent name while CARR remains its first tenant and launch branding configuration?
recommendation: Yes. Select an independent platform name before production construction creates more CARR-prefixed product, package, environment, domain, and interface commitments. Keep CARR as the launch tenant/customer configuration and preserve familiar CARR-facing labels through a planned transition until Joe approves the final name.
criteria: platform and IP independence from Joe's current employer
migration cost before versus after construction
domain, trademark, package, and app-store availability

options.option: Keep CARR as the permanent platform name
options.tradeoff: Avoids change now but permanently ties Joe-owned platform identity to the current employer and makes later licensing or departure awkward.

options.option: Choose an independent platform name now; configure CARR as the launch tenant

scores.migration_effort_now: bounded Phase 0 metadata and later planned cutover

options.tradeoff: Requires a deliberate naming and cutover decision now but prevents much larger identity debt and preserves CARR as a customer configuration rather than the platform owner.

options.option: Use a neutral internal codename and choose the public platform name after the pilot
options.tradeoff: Defers trademark and domain pressure but risks two renames and ambiguous doctrine, code, and interface vocabulary.

proposed_identity_architecture.platform_name: TBD by council recommendation and Joe approval
proposed_identity_architecture.platform_owner: Joe retains platform, IP, root, release, and licensing authority
proposed_identity_architecture.tenant_branding: CARR may remain visible as the organization, tenant, and familiar launch configuration without being the underlying software name
product_pattern: Doc as the human-facing assistant identity unless separately renamed
proposed_identity_architecture.runtime_pattern: Hermes may power Doc and routine orchestration, but runtime/vendor names do not become the platform name or source of truth
proposed_identity_architecture.commercial_boundary: No public SaaS, signup, billing, tenant selector, marketplace, or commercial rollout is authorized by renaming

required_before_final_name: Joe states desired brand tone and whether Doc remains the assistant name
trademark and corporate-name screening in relevant jurisdictions
GitHub, package registry, Apple bundle ID, and app-store collision screening
confusing-similarity review against AI, software, healthcare, and real-estate products
spoken, written, accessibility, and partner comprehension test

cutover_contract.before_approval: Do not rename canonical roadmap records, production domains, databases, repository, packages, cookies, OAuth audiences, or deployed products.
cutover_contract.after_approval: Amend all three roadmaps and the maturity baseline in one controlled revision; add a versioned old-to-new vocabulary map; classify each CARR-prefixed identifier as tenant-facing alias, internal compatibility identifier, or rename target; preserve redirects and audit provenance; verify Joe and Dell journeys before retiring old labels.
cutover_contract.acceptance: No new product-layer contract may assume CARR is the immutable platform identity. Tenant context remains server-derived, and the launch tenant can be branded CARR without choosing platform authority or granting source control.

council_question: Recommend the independent-platform naming architecture now and authorize a bounded name-selection sprint after Joe approves the council output, or retain CARR as the permanent software identity?
proposed_council_language: Approve the architecture in which the Joe-owned software platform receives an independent name and CARR becomes its first tenant and launch branding configuration. This decision does not choose the final name or authorize public SaaS. Final selection requires trademark, domain, registry, app-store, similarity, usability, and cutover evidence, followed by Joe approval and one controlled roadmap vocabulary revision.
